sourceType: Independent original practice questions based on publicly listed exam or MCQ topics; not verbatim UNISA paper questions
sourceLimitations: These are newly written MCQs based on themes in the linked public source, not exact original paper wording. Some source previews are incomplete. Use the Source link to view the original where available.

questions.text: Which business application is most suitable for managing repeat customer interactions?
questions.explanation:
CRM collects customer history and contact details to support stronger customer service and relationships.

Student note: Customer relationships are managed through CRM, not by a knowledge base alone.

questions.text: A company records expert troubleshooting steps so new employees can solve familiar problems. Which system fits best?
questions.explanation:
Knowledge management helps organisations capture, organise and reuse know-how.

Student note: KMS = reusable organisational knowledge.

questions.text: A business hires a provider to maintain an older software application. Which practice is being used?
questions.explanation:
Outsourcing means a third party delivers services or development work under contract.

Student note: Outsourcing can cover maintenance as well as new development.

questions.text: Which internet service uses pages with links to present information?
questions.explanation:
The Web is an information service that uses the Internet and web standards to present linked resources.

Student note: Internet = underlying network; Web = service running over it.

options: A worldwide interconnection of networks using common protocols
questions.correctAnswer: A worldwide interconnection of networks using common protocols
questions.explanation:
The internet connects many networks and supports services such as websites, email and file transfer.

Student note: Internet and World Wide Web are related but not identical.

questions.text: What part of an application allows a user to enter commands and see results?
questions.explanation:
A user interface is the point where a person interacts with a system through screens, controls or other input methods.

Student note: UI design affects usability and the number of mistakes people make.

questions.text: Employees resist a replacement ordering system. Which management activity should help address the resistance?
questions.explanation:
Change management includes communication, training and support to help people adopt new ways of working.

Student note: A technically correct system can fail if users reject it.

questions.text: Which project stage describes how a proposed system will be built to meet the identified requirements?
questions.explanation:
Design turns requirements into plans for components, interfaces, data and processing.

Student note: Analysis asks what is needed; design explains how to build it.

questions.text: Which concept concerns safe, comfortable and effective interaction between people and computers in the workplace?
questions.explanation:
Ergonomics studies how work tools and environments fit human needs, including posture and interface design.

Student note: Think people, health, workspace and ease of use.

questions.text: Which system supports a group of managers who must discuss and choose a solution together?
questions.explanation:
GDSS provides tools that help multiple people share information, examine choices and reach group decisions.

Student note: GDSS is group-focused; DSS can support individual decision making.

questions.text: Which project document specifies what information a proposed system must provide, to whom and when?
questions.explanation:
Information requirements identify the information users and processes need to operate effectively.

Student note: Know users, required information, timing and access needs.

questions.text: A supplier is granted secure access to part of a retailer's internal ordering system. What is this called?
questions.explanation:
An extranet provides approved external partners controlled access to company information.

Student note: Internal only = intranet; selected outsiders = extranet.
